messages:
anya.r: Heads-up: running into flaky errors in our FastAPI sample when tests call the app startup multiple times (pytest-asyncio + uvicorn in-process). Repro attached.

liam.t: what errors are you seeing?

anya.r: sometimes tests fail with RuntimeError: Event loop is closed or ConnectionResetError from httpcore. Happens when the SDK's AsyncClient is created in the app startup handler and tests run multiple isolated loops. Minimal excerpt below.

anya.r: ```py
# conftest.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from httpx import AsyncClient

app = FastAPI()

@app.on_event("startup")
async def startup():
    app.state.client = AsyncClient(base_url="http://localhost:8000")

@app.on_event("shutdown")
async def shutdown():
    await app.state.client.aclose()

# tests call TestClient / anyio which spins loops; if the startup client outlives the loop you get errors
```

olivia.m: yep that's the common pitfall: AsyncClient binds transports to the loop it was created on. FastAPI startup may be called under a different loop when tests manage their own event loop policy.

liam.t: two options: 1) create the client lazily inside request handlers, 2) use lifespan/context-managed client created by the same loop that will use it. For tests, the simplest is to wire the client as an async context var in the app lifespan so creation and close happen within the test loop.

liam.t: example lifespan pattern:````py
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app):
    client = AsyncClient()
    app.state.client = client
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        await client.aclose()
```

anya.r: thanks. two follow-ups: 1) can the py-sdk provide a helper to make this less error-prone for new users? Something like `AsyncClient.for_lifespan()` or `create_async_client(lifecycle="lifespan")` so docs/samples don't encourage import-time clients. 2) our type checker (pyright) is unhappy about our wrapper's async context manager types on the SDK class.

olivia.m: +1 for helper. For typing, annotate __aenter__ and __aexit__ explicitly and inherit from `typing.AsyncContextManager["AsyncClient"]` or implement `async def __aenter__(self) -> "AsyncClient":`. That clears pyright/mypy.

liam.t: we should also add a small note in the sample-app README under "Do not create AsyncClient at import time" and show a one-liner to get the safe pattern. Many users copy examples verbatim.

anya.r: filed a gist with a failing test and logs: https://gist.github.com/anya/fastapi-asyncclient-test-repro

devx-bot: Created issue RDW-789: "py-sdk: helper + docs for safe AsyncClient lifecycle (lifespan/test friendly) & typing fixes" and assigned to olivia.m. :robot_face:

olivia.m: i'll pick up RDW-789. plan: add `AsyncClient.for_lifespan()` that returns an AsyncContextManager, update sample-app to use lifespan, and add explicit return types for __aenter__/__aexit__ in wrapper. i'll also add a short note in the tests section about pytest-asyncio/anyio loop policies.

anya.r: appreciated — that should save new users a lot of puzzling flakes. :+1:

liam.t: FYI we may want to also provide a `sync_client()` helper that wraps calls for sync codepaths (for simple scripts) so people don't try to reuse an async client from sync code.

olivia.m: good call. adding that to the issue.

anya.r: thanks everyone — i'll update the PR for the sample app after RDW-789 lands.
